Kill switch is off: if the core fails, traffic goes out directly

Per-app bypass: the selected apps never use the VPN
Per-app proxy: apps that are not selected never use the VPN
LAN bypass: local network addresses are reached outside the VPN
No known leak path is open for the current settings.
The system lockdown state is read when the VPN starts. Start the VPN once to check it; Android 9 and older never report it.

When the VPN core fails or stops on its own, the kill switch keeps the tunnel open with nothing behind it, so traffic is dropped instead of going out over your normal network, and the app keeps trying to reconnect. It works only while this app is running in VPN mode.
The only full protection: Always-on VPN

Android itself can block every connection that does not go through the VPN, even during boot, after the app is killed and when another VPN app tries to take over. Open System VPN settings, tap the gear next to v2rayNG, and turn on both \"Always-on VPN\" and \"Block connections without VPN\".

After the phone starts there is no tunnel until this app starts it, and apps can connect directly in the meantime. Without the system lockdown, keep mobile data and Wi-Fi off until the VPN is connected; \"Connect after device boot\" shortens the gap but does not close it.

Android allows one VPN at a time. When another VPN app connects, Android disconnects this one and no app can prevent it; you get a notice when it happens. The system lockdown stops other VPN apps from taking over.
Per-app proxy, LAN bypass and direct rules

Apps excluded by per-app proxy, and local network addresses when LAN bypass is on, always use your normal network. Routing rules that send sites \"direct\" show your real IP to those sites. Exclude only what you trust.

Devices connected to the phone\'s system hotspot or USB tethering do not go through the VPN on Android; they use your real connection. Use VPN sharing in this app, or LAN sharing on a rooted phone, to send their traffic through the tunnel.
The kill switch exists only in VPN mode. In proxy-only mode, apps that ignore the proxy go out directly; in root mode, protection depends on the routing rules. Use VPN mode for leak protection.
The VPN hides your IP address, not your position. GPS, nearby Wi-Fi and cell towers, the SIM card, time zone and language can still reveal where you are. Deny location to apps you do not trust.

What can still reveal your location
No known signal contradicts the virtual position.

1. Turn on Developer options: Settings > About phone, tap "Build number" seven times.
2. In Developer options, tap "Select mock location app" and choose v2rayNG.
3. Choose a position here, ideally with "Match the VPN country", and switch Virtual location on.
4. Connect the VPN to a server in the same country and set the phone's time zone to that country.

Apps can ask Android whether a position is simulated, and many banking, game and delivery apps do. Your SIM card, the mobile network, nearby Wi-Fi networks and cell towers, Google\'s location history and your account settings can all reveal the real country. For the best result use Wi-Fi without a SIM card, turn off Wi-Fi and Bluetooth scanning and Google Location Accuracy, and keep the time zone, language and VPN country consistent with the virtual position.
v2rayNG is not the selected mock location app, so apps still get the real position

Let other phones, tablets and computers use this VPN. Without root, the app opens its own Wi-Fi network and the other devices set this phone as their proxy; anything that does not use the proxy has no internet at all, so nothing leaks. With root, the system hotspot, USB and Ethernet tethering go through the VPN with no setup on the other device.
The VPN is not connected. Connect it first, otherwise the other devices get no internet.
Opens a Wi-Fi network for other devices and lets them use the VPN through the proxy
QR code to join the sharing Wi-Fi
No local network address yet. Turn on Wi-Fi sharing, or connect this phone and the other device to the same Wi-Fi.
Proxy type: SOCKS5 and HTTP on the same port.

The proxy has no password. On the sharing Wi-Fi only people with its password can reach it, but on a shared Wi-Fi anyone could use your VPN. Set a SOCKS user name and password in Settings to prevent that.

Join the Wi-Fi above (scan the QR code with the camera), then set the proxy to the address and port shown:
• Android: Wi-Fi > the network > Edit > Advanced > Proxy: Manual.
• iPhone/iPad: Settings > Wi-Fi > ⓘ > Configure Proxy: Manual.
• Windows: Settings > Network & internet > Proxy > Use a proxy server.
• macOS: System Settings > Network > Wi-Fi > Details > Proxies.
Apps and games that ignore the system proxy will not work through sharing; use a proxy-aware client (for example v2rayN or v2rayNG with a SOCKS server) on the other device for full coverage.
Routes devices on the system hotspot, USB and Ethernet tethering through the VPN; no proxy setup needed. Applies from the next VPN start.
Sharing with a computer over cable

With root: turn on Full sharing, connect the computer by USB and enable USB tethering (or Ethernet tethering with an adapter); the computer\'s traffic goes through the VPN. Without root: connect the computer to the sharing Wi-Fi, or to the same Wi-Fi as this phone, and set the proxy shown above. Without root, Android\'s own hotspot and USB tethering bypass the VPN.
